_comment: Expeditions: off-screen squad jobs sent from the Guildhall (key E). stats: the stats that count and how much (squad strength = sum of stat x weight over the squad). target: the strength that gives a 50% chance; every point above or below moves it by Empire.EXPEDITION_PER_POINT. danger 1-3 drives injuries (and, at 3, a rare loss). rations: Supplies per person sent. reward: [min, max] per resource, or a flat number; fray: change to the job's province on success; recruit: who joins on success (the job disappears once they have joined). needs: guildhall level, erased (the province must be erased) and tags used by traits (blank, concord). standing: faction standing change on success (standing_fail: on failure). text: {a} {b} = two squad members, {lead} = the first one picked, {squad} = everyone.

jobs.name: Forage the Frayed Meadow
jobs.blurb: Half the Meadow has gone pale, but the turnips in the other half don't know that yet. Dig fast, don't look at the white bits.

success: {a} and {b} came back with sacks of turnips, a wheel of cheese and a goat nobody admits stealing.
{lead} found a cellar the Blank had skipped. It was full of pickles. It is now empty of pickles.
fail: {a} dug up a turnip that had gone white inside. Everyone dropped everything and ran. The sacks are still out there.
The field kept getting longer the further {lead} walked. They came back with one onion and a headache.

jobs.name: Salvage at Old Mill Crossing
jobs.blurb: The old millers left in a hurry. Their gears, nails and strongboxes did not. Bring a crowbar and a straight face.

success: {a} pried open a strongbox while {b} held the door shut against something that turned out to be wind. Good haul.
{lead} took the mill apart down to the nails and sold the nails back to the people who live nearby.
fail: The millwheel started turning on its own. {a} and {b} decided the gears could stay where they were.
{lead} fell through the granary floor into a smaller, older granary. Climbing out took most of the trip.

jobs.name: Escort a barge to Gallows Ferry
jobs.blurb: A Guild barge needs bodies on deck. The pay is good because the river is not. Mercenaries respect people who show up.

success: River bandits tried the barge once. {a} threw one of them back. {b} threw the rest. The Guild paid in full and nearly smiled.
{lead} stood at the prow looking menacing for two days straight. It worked. Nobody even tried.
fail: The barge was fine. The cargo was fine. {a} fell in, {b} went in after them, and the Guild docked the pay for 'swimming on contract time'.
Bandits in the reeds. {lead} held them off but the cargo didn't make it. Half pay, and a lecture.

jobs.name: Scout the Saltreed edge
jobs.blurb: The marsh is fraying fast. Someone should walk its edge, mark the paths that still hold and stake lanterns where the white starts.

success: {a} mapped the paths that still hold while {b} hammered stakes where the marsh went quiet. Saltreed frays a little slower for it.
{lead} walked the whole edge and came back with a notebook full of drawings. Some of the drawings were drawn back.
fail: The paths moved while {a} was mapping them. {b} says the map now shows a different marsh. Possibly a better one.
{lead} got lost in fog that was not quite fog. Found by the smell of Tobble's stew, two days later.

jobs.name: Rumour: a witch in the Gutterwoods
jobs.blurb: Woodcutters say a hedge-witch is selling cures out of a hollow tree, and the Coven wants her gone. Find her before they do. Bring coin; she will ask.

success: {a} found the hollow tree. {b} drank the tea before anyone could stop them and is mostly fine. Mother Gristle agreed to come, for a fee to be named later.
{lead} talked Mother Gristle out of her tree with promises of steady work and sick people. She seemed delighted by the sick people.
fail: The witch sold {a} a 'map' and {b} a 'cure'. The map led in a circle. The cure was for a disease {b} now has.
Coven sentries turned {lead} around at the treeline. Politely. With knives.

jobs.name: Rumour: a scribe hiding in Lampwick
jobs.blurb: A runaway from the Abbey is hiding in the Lampwick hills with a stolen page that will not stay written. The Abbey wants the page back, and the scribe.

success: {a} found Sister Abeyance by following the sound of someone arguing with a piece of paper. {b} carried her books. All of them.
{lead} traded the Abbey trackers a forged page for the real scribe. Sister Abeyance says the page liked {lead}. That is new.
fail: {a} and {b} found the cave, a cold fire and a note that said 'not yet'. The note was in {a}'s handwriting.
The Abbey's trackers got there first. {lead} came home with nothing but a strongly worded pamphlet.

jobs.name: Rumour: a deserter on Tithe Road
jobs.blurb: A Concord corporal walked out on an Erasure order and is hiding somewhere along the Tithe Road toll posts. The Concord has posted a reward. Pay it to yourself.

success: {a} waved forged papers at the toll post while {b} walked out the back with Corporal Daro, who complained about the paperwork the entire way home.
{lead} found Daro in a ditch, sharpening a sword and insulting a crow. Daro says yes, mainly to annoy the Concord.
fail: The Concord asked {a} to fill in a form explaining the visit. Then another form explaining the first form. {b} gave up on day two.
{lead} found the ditch, the sword and the crow. No Daro. The crow was very rude about it.

jobs.name: Skim the paper edge at Whitewater
jobs.blurb: Whitewater is gone, but the Blank leaves Ink pooled at its edges like a tide line. Scoop it up and do not let it read you back.

success: {a} skimmed Ink off the white while {b} kept talking, loudly, so the Blank would know they were still there. It works. Nobody knows why.
{lead} came back with jars of Ink and an extra shadow. The shadow left after a bath.
fail: The white got hungry. {a} dropped the jars and pulled {b} back by the collar. {b} has a pale stripe in their hair now and will not discuss it.
{lead} stared too long. Came back fine, apart from forgetting the word for 'spoon'. Nobody has had the heart to tell them.

jobs.name: Buy Back the Paper
jobs.blurb: The broker who holds Bran's contract keeps a counting-house on Gallows Ferry. Bran wants to buy himself back, or rewrite the terms, or throw the man in the river. He has not decided.

success: Brannoc paid the broker, then made him strike his own name off the tattoo. {squad} watched the pen go into the river. Nobody was thrown in. Narrowly.
The broker tried to raise the price. Brannoc leaned on the counter until it broke. The price came down. So did the counter.
fail: The broker was out. His three large nephews were in. {squad} came home bruised, with Brannoc's contract still very much held.
The broker sold the contract on again while {squad} were still on the road. Brannoc has a new name to find, and a new reason to be angry.

jobs.name: Collect from Hester Vane
jobs.blurb: Coven elder Hester Vane owes Mother Gristle a life, and has for eleven years. Gristle is going to collect: not coin, but her name back on the Coven's tree.

success: Gristle reminded Hester of the fever, the grandson and the bill. Hester wept, then carved Gristle's name on the tree herself. {squad} were offered tea. Nobody drank it.
Hester's nephews met {squad} at the treeline. Gristle met the nephews with a bottle. By evening her name was back on the tree.
fail: Hester would not come out of her hut. Gristle left a bill nailed to the door. {squad} were chased out by bees, which may have been the Coven's answer.
The Coven met in council and voted Gristle out again, for old times' sake. She charged them for the meeting.

jobs.name: Find Hob's Wick
jobs.blurb: The village Daro refused to strike out lies off the Tithe Road, past toll posts with Daro's face on the posters. They need to know if it is still there.

success: Hob's Wick is still there: mill turning, goats loose, beer bad. In the chapel, a plaque mourns "Corporal Daro, fallen against the Blank". Daro did not correct anybody.
{squad} found the village by the smell of the mill. Daro stood in the square for a long time. Then they bought everyone a round.
fail: A toll post recognised the hood. {squad} spent the trip filling in forms explaining the hood.
Fog on the Tithe Road. {squad} walked in circles around a village they could hear but not find. Daro says that is worse than white.

jobs.name: Correct the Original
jobs.blurb: Quill's original ledger, with thirty-one people written off in Quill's own hand, sits in a Concord strongbox at Old Mill Crossing. Quill wants to correct it. Nobody else can forge Quill.

success: {squad} pried the strongbox open. Quill sat in the dust with the good pen and changed thirty-one lines from "written off" to "carried forward".
The strongbox had a lock, a ward and a very bored clerk. Quill bribed the clerk with a better job. The ledger is corrected.
fail: The strongbox had already been moved, by a clerk with a cart and no forwarding address. Quill is drafting a strongly worded memo.
{squad} opened the wrong strongbox. It was full of other people's sins. Quill read them all, put them back and came home quiet.

jobs.name: Fetch the Last Drop's Sign
jobs.blurb: Tobble's old tavern in the Frayed Meadow is a roofless ruin at the Blank's edge, but its sign still hangs. He wants it back before the white does. Pack a ladder.

success: {squad} got the sign down a minute before the doorstep went white. Tobble carried it home himself, complaining about his knees the whole way, smiling the whole way.
The cellar was still there under the ruin. {squad} came back with the sign and two barrels Tobble swears are vintage.
fail: The ladder went pale halfway up. {squad} got down in a hurry. The sign is still hanging, and it's closer to the white now.
Tobble's knees gave out on the ridge. {squad} carried him home, sign-less. He has not stopped apologising, which is worse than complaining.

jobs.name: Follow the Page
jobs.blurb: Sister Abeyance's page drew a map: the Lampwick Hills, a chapel nobody remembers, and an X. The page has never been this direct. She has to follow it.

success: {squad} found the chapel exactly where the page said, though it was not there the first time they looked. Abeyance came out with a slip of paper and would not say what it said until she got home.
The page led {squad} up a path that kept apologising for being steep. At the top: a chapel, a lectern, a book with one page missing. Not any more.
fail: The map changed halfway. {squad} followed it to a duck pond. The page seemed pleased with itself.
{squad} found the chapel, but the door would not open. A voice inside said, very politely, "not today".

pairs.text: Old soldiers: Bran and Daro cover each other's blind side
Two ex-Concord: they know where the forms are weakest
Pell and Abeyance both talk to the dead; the dead give directions
Quill and Tobble argue about Tobble's bar tab the whole way
Gristle bills Bran for every bandage; Bran refuses on principle
